description:
We are a team of five enthusiastic and creative students: Huda, Atifa, Manaswitha, Yoshitha, and Harshitha. We are passionate about space, science, technology, and innovation. Our team brings skills in research, creativity, problem-solving, presentation, and teamwork, with an interest in exploring AI and technology to develop innovative solutions.

We are looking for team members with skills in coding, web development, data analysis, AI/ML, and space science who are passionate about learning..
summary: For the NASA Space Apps Challenge, Team Orbit Keepers developed "Abandoned But Not Forgotten," an interactive digital publication and educational platform dedicated to exploring historic spacecraft and scientific equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars.   What we developed: We built a clean, professional daylight-themed website featuring an eight-part digital monograph, human-grade voice narration, embedded NASA/JPL/CNRS/ESA video archives, and a comparative Mission Matrix table. This is supported by a comprehensive presentation deck and PowerPoint slides.   How it addresses the challenge: The platform preserves the history of surface relics—from Apollo 11 to the Opportunity rover—making planetary science accessible through modern web design, text-to-speech audio, and multimedia archives.   Why it is important: Created collaboratively by our team members across multiple grades (Huda in 8th, Atifa in 6th, Manaswitha and Yoshitha in 7th, Harshitha in 9th, and Asma in 10th), our project demonstrates how historical space hardware continues to provide reference baselines and educational inspiration for the future of space exploration.
details: Abandoned But Not Forgotten is an interactive digital publication and educational website that tells the stories of historic spacecraft, rovers, and scientific instruments left behind on the Moon and Mars. The website allows users to explore an eight-part digital book, listen to chapters through voice narration, watch official mission videos from NASA, JPL, CNRS, and ESA, and view a Mission Matrix that compares different space missions. It transforms historical information into an interesting and engaging learning experience for students and space enthusiasts by combining facts, audio, videos, and interactive features. The main aim of the project is to educate people about planetary science and inspire future generations to explore space. It highlights how, even though these machines are no longer active, their scientific contributions continue to support modern space exploration. We developed the website using HTML5, JavaScript, and Tailwind CSS, along with the Web Speech API for text-to-speech narration. We also created a PowerPoint presentation and visual design layouts. The creative part of our project is the combination of a digital book's appearance with modern website features, including smooth navigation, audio indicators, and connected mission information. Our team consists of Huda (8th grade), Atifa (6th grade), Manaswitha (7th grade), Yoshitha (7th grade), Harshitha (9th grade), and Asma Kulsum (10th grade). While developing the project, we focused on historical accuracy, accessibility, easy navigation, and a clean, attractive design that works smoothly across different devices.
